title: Free will and decree
hookLine: two verses side by side, and the theologians who tried to hold them both

cards: The caliph Umar is on the road to Syria when word comes: plague has broken out in the land ahead. He hears his advisers disagree, and decides to turn back. Abu Ubayda, a companion of the Prophet, objects.
Are you running from the decree of Allah? Umar's answer is in Sahih al-Bukhari: yes, we run from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah.
If your camels came down into a valley with one green side and one bare one, wouldn't you graze them by Allah's decree whichever side you chose? The theologians made this a hard question.
If Allah decrees everything, what's left for my choice? And if my choice is real, what's left for His decree?

teach.b: Start with two verses, in Pickthall's translation. One says: "Then whosoever will, let him believe, and whosoever will, let him disbelieve." A real choice, handed to us.

teach.h: YE WILL NOT, UNLESS ALLAH WILLETH.
teach.b: Another says: "Yet ye will not, unless Allah willeth." Every choice resting inside His will.
The Qur'an puts both on the page and doesn't apologize for either, and the theologians of this part each tried to hold them together.

The Mu'tazilah leaned on the first: a just God only judges people for acts truly their own, so humans bring their acts into being. The Ash'aris leaned on another verse: "When Allah hath created you and what ye make?"
Allah creates every act, they said, and the human being acquires it, takes it on, and is answerable for it. Their word is kasb, acquisition.
The Maturidis said Allah creates the act, the human being's free choice is real, and it's that choice that is judged.

teach.h: KASB, AND A MATTER BETWEEN THE TWO.
teach.b: And Shia theology has a saying it traces to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq: neither compulsion nor complete handing over, but a matter between the two. None of them says we're puppets, and none says Allah steps aside.
Each is trying to keep both verses true at once. And Umar's answer at the edge of the plague is one anyone can use: even choosing the green side of the valley sits inside the decree.

teach.h: DO YOUR PART. LET IT REST.
teach.b: Do your part with your whole effort, then let the outcome rest with Allah.

how: Muslims affirm both Allah's decree and human responsibility, and the schools of theology explain how they fit in different ways, from the Ash'ari teaching of kasb to the Shia saying of 'a matter between the two'.

games.q: what does “free will and decree” mean?
o: a Shia saying from Imam Ja'far about the imams' guidance
how human choice and Allah's decree fit together, both kept true
a ruling on when it's allowed to flee a town hit by plague

games.q: free will and decree — tap the pairs.
p: the Ash'ari word: acquiring an act
humans bring their own acts into being
Umar at the edge of the plague

s: the Qur'an speaks only of decree, never of choice
it says whosoever will, let him believe, and also that ye will not unless Allah willeth.
Ash'aris say Allah creates acts and humans acquire them
their word for it is kasb, and the human is answerable.
Umar turning back from the plague was running from Allah's decree
he said he was running from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah.

games.q: you're Umar. plague is in the land ahead, and a companion asks: are you running from the decree of Allah? what do you say?
o: no, I'll go on; whatever is decreed will happen.
yes: from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah.
decree has nothing to do with it.
games.why: in Sahih al-Bukhari, Umar runs from decree to decree, like a herder choosing the green side of a valley over the bare one.

practice: Bring to mind one small good thing you could do, a message you've been putting off, a dish someone else usually washes, and choose it on purpose, the way Umar chose his road.
Then picture the moment after, and let go of how it lands; that part isn't yours to hold. If you pray, you can hand the outcome to Allah in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Free will and decree. How human choice and Allah's decree fit together: a question the schools answer in different ways, each keeping both true. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: acquisition, earning; the Ash'ari term for how a person takes on an act.

carryVoice: Your line: choose, and trust. The effort is yours; the outcome rests with Allah. I'll be here tomorrow.
